# SkillDrift: get the job you want and grow your career
URL: https://www.skilldrift.ai/
Summary: Upload your resume free. See jobs and internships scored out of 100 and the skills holding you back, then learn them: your resume updates itself and your job matches re-score as you grow. No account needed to see your score.

## Get the job you want. Then grow into the next one.
SkillDrift finds jobs and internships scored out of 100 for you, plans what to learn and gets you ready to apply and interview. Every step you finish raises your scores, and after you get the role it keeps going.

AI courses
## A free AI course for your field. Then the AI your jobs ask for.
Most AI courses are the same for everyone. SkillDrift starts from your field, then from the jobs you actually match, so you learn the AI employers in your role are asking for right now.
- Free, for your field Your first AI course is on us, built for your field, such as AI for Field Sales or AI for Electronics and Communication. Finish it and the certificate goes into your resume.
- Then AI for your exact role SkillDrift reads the jobs you match. When enough of them ask for AI tools such as ChatGPT, Copilot or generative AI, it builds an AI course for your role, such as AI tools for data analysts.
- You see why before you pay How many of your jobs ask, for example 24 of your 60, with lines quoted from two employers. 50 credits, or included in Active Seeker.

Resume rewrite
## Your resume says what you did. It should say what happened.
Almost every resume lists duties. Every hiring manager scans for outcomes. SkillDrift asks you what actually happened, then rewrites each line around the result (the number, the scale, the change) and formats it so the ATS can read it.
Before
“Worked on a college project using Python and machine learning.”
After
“Built a churn-prediction model in Python across 40,000 customer records, reaching 82% precision, shipped as capstone for a six-person team.”
Before
“Responsible for managing vendor relationships and procurement.”
After
“Renegotiated 14 vendor contracts across two regions, cutting annual spend 18% without switching a single supplier.”
Before
“Led the engineering team and was involved in technical strategy.”
After
“Grew engineering from 9 to 34 across three squads; cut median deploy time from 40 minutes to 6 and halved release failures.”
### It asks you. It never invents.
SkillDrift asks a short set of questions and rewrites from your answers. Every figure on your resume is one you supplied, nothing is generated, so nothing can surprise you in an interview.
### Your ATS score moves with it
The rewrite fixes structure and parsing at the same time, so the resume reads well to both a machine and a person.
### Your original stays untouched
The rewrite becomes your new master copy only if you accept it. Side-by-side comparison before you commit.
Upload your resume - free See a real rewrite, before and after
Everything in the loop
## Seven powerful tools, seamlessly connected in one unified system.
Every tool feeds into one connected profile, one growing score, and one resume that gets stronger with every skill you build. Each links to its own page.
01 Resume tailoring Tailor your resume to one job without rewriting it from scratch.
SkillDrift keeps one master resume and generates a fresh ATS-optimised version for each job you apply to. What changes is emphasis and ordering. Every figure on the tailored version is one you supplied, and your master copy is never altered. Seeing how your resume reads to the bots, as a four level ATS band, costs nothing.
See resume tailoring
02 Resume rewrite Rewrite your resume around what happened, not what you were responsible for.
Most resumes list duties. SkillDrift reads each line, asks what actually resulted from it, and rewrites it around the outcome. It never invents a number: every figure comes from you. The result is the same job history reading as evidence rather than as a job description.
See resume rewrite
03 Interview prep Practise the interview out loud, and get an honest score out of 10.
A chatbot can ask you questions in text. A real interview is spoken, under time pressure, with follow-up questions. SkillDrift runs mock interviews in text, recorded voice and live voice, and the live interview runs in English and in Hindi. Every report gives a score out of 10, your hire chance and the questions to work on first, and every weak answer can become a learning roadmap.
See interview prep
04 Job matching See which jobs you can get now, and what to learn for the rest.
SkillDrift reads your resume against each open role and scores the match out of 100, with the reasons behind the number named rather than hidden. Internships and entry level roles are included for anyone with under a year of experience. Basic analysis on any role costs nothing.
See job matching
05 Career roadmap Build a career plan from your resume, for the role you actually want.
Pick the role you want and SkillDrift reads your current resume against it, names every skill standing between the two, and orders them by which one moves your readiness most. The path itself is free. Building the full roadmap, with the learning attached to each gap, is 50 credits.
See career roadmap
06 Skill benchmarking See exactly which skills are missing between you and the role you want.
SkillDrift reads your resume against the role you actually want and names every missing skill individually, rather than returning one overall percentage. Your named gaps and your ATS resume score as a four level band come back without creating an account, and every job and internship is scored out of 100 against your actual skills.
See skill benchmarking
07 Learning sprints Close one named skill gap at a time, in short sprints.
A learning sprint is built from a gap your own report named, not from a catalogue. It is short enough to finish, and when you finish it the certificate writes itself into your resume and your readiness percentage moves. Building the roadmap that produces the sprints is 50 credits, the learning content itself is free, and the certificate is 50.
See learning sprints

Past roughly eight applications a month, or three live mock interviews, Active Seeker costs you less. If you are in an active search, take Active Seeker; if you are learning at your own pace, take Casual User.

FAQ
## The questions people actually ask before signing up.
What is SkillDrift?
SkillDrift is an AI career platform that scores your skills against the role you want, builds the learning path that closes the gap, and matches you to jobs and internships rated out of 100. As you learn, your score re-scores itself and your resume updates automatically.
Is SkillDrift free?
The parts that tell you where you stand are free forever: skill gap analysis, a career path, resume and ATS analysis, job matching, jobs and internships, one AI course for your domain, industry news and podcasts. New accounts also get 160 credits, enough to rewrite your resume, tailor it to a job and download it.
Can SkillDrift analyse my resume without signing up?
Yes. Drop your resume on the homepage and you get your readiness score, the three skills holding it down, and three matched roles, with no account. Signing up shows the full gap report, every match and your roadmap, and your resume carries across so you never upload it twice.
Does SkillDrift invent numbers on my resume?
No. SkillDrift asks you a short set of questions about what each achievement actually produced, and rewrites from your answers. Every figure on your resume is one you supplied, so nothing can surprise you in an interview.
What does a credit cost, and what does it buy?
A Casual User pack of 299 credits costs ₹299 ($6.99 outside India), and credits you buy never expire. Tailoring your resume to a job is 18 credits, a Deep fit analysis is 37, a text-based mock interview is 50, a learning roadmap is 50, a resume download is 54 to 70, and a full outcome rewrite is 70. Active Seeker, with no credit counting, is ₹599 ($15.99 outside India) a month.
Can I use SkillDrift if I am a student or a fresher?
Yes. We carry internships and roles for people with under a year of experience, scored the same way as everything else, so you can see where you genuinely stand rather than guessing.
What happens when I finish a course?
The certificate is added to your resume automatically, with no re-uploading and no re-formatting. Share it to LinkedIn in one click, as a post or straight into your certifications section, and the 50 credits it cost to issue come back to you.
Is the learning on SkillDrift personalised to me?
Yes. SkillDrift starts from the gaps your resume, a job description or a mock interview shows, and builds each learning roadmap around those gaps and the role you are aiming at. When you finish, your gaps and job scores update and the certificate is added to your resume. We call this closed loop career development.
Is there a free AI course on SkillDrift?
Yes. Your first AI course is free and built for your field, such as AI for Field Sales or AI for Electronics and Communication, and the certificate goes into your resume when you finish. SkillDrift also reads the jobs you match in your own role. When enough of them ask for AI tools, it builds an AI course for that role, such as AI tools for data analysts, and shows you the postings that ask for it. That course is 50 credits, or included in Active Seeker.
How is this different from a resume builder?
A resume builder formats what you already wrote. SkillDrift starts from the role you want, tells you what is missing, helps you close it, and keeps your resume current as you do. The resume is an output of the loop, not the product.
I finished courses but I am still not getting interviews. Why?
Usually the course did not match what the jobs you apply to ask for, or it never reached your resume. SkillDrift starts from those jobs: each one is scored out of 100 and the missing skills are named, so your upskilling goes where it counts. Finish and verify a roadmap and the certificate is written into your resume, and every job that asks for that skill re-scores by the amount shown before you started. We call this skill compounding: every real step adds to the same scores.
How much does finishing a course raise my scores?
Each roadmap shows how much it will raise your readiness before you start. Finish and verify it, and readiness rises by exactly that amount, along with every job that asks for that skill. SkillDrift shows you the number rather than promising that one course makes you job ready.
How does SkillDrift help me apply for jobs?
Open the Apply Kit on any job and SkillDrift prepares the application: a resume tailored to the job, a cover note, answers to the questions it asks and help asking for a referral. It checks the job is still open first, and a day or two later asks whether you applied, so your job board stays right.
Why did a job disappear from my matches?
It closed, or it was posted more than 30 days ago. SkillDrift hides those jobs and never charges for one. Jobs you have already applied to stay on your board.

# How SkillDrift works - the closed career loop
URL: https://www.skilldrift.ai/how-it-works
Summary: Upload, get scored out of 100, follow a roadmap, earn certificates that write themselves into your resume, and watch your match score rise. Free to start.

- SkillDrift
- How it works
The closed loop
## Most tools hand you one piece. SkillDrift closes the loop.
Every other product gives you one arc of the circle: a course library, a resume builder, a job board. The loop is why your score moves instead of your bookmarks piling up. What is closed loop career development?
Upload your resume - free See what's free
Six steps, then round again
## How one turn of the loop actually runs.
Nothing here needs a form filled in. Each step produces the input the next one needs, and the last step feeds the first.
- 01
### Upload
We read your skills straight from your resume. No forms to fill.
- 02
### Score
Pick a target role and see your match out of 100, with each missing skill named.
- 03
### Roadmap
The exact skills to close it, in the order that moves your score.
- 04
### Learn
Short sprints built from your own gaps and sized to your hours.
- 05
### Certify
Finish a course and the certificate writes itself into your resume.
- 06
### Rise
Your score re-scores itself free, and better roles unlock. Then round again.
What moves your scores
## What moves your scores, and by how much?
A chat starts from zero every time. SkillDrift keeps one record, so every step you take changes something you can see.
### Finish a roadmap
Your readiness, and every job that asks for that skill, rises by the amount the roadmap showed before you started. Once.
### Practise an interview
Your report names the weak answers, and each one can become a roadmap of its own.
### Work in your role
Each month in a role adds to the skills it uses, and a logged win can go onto your resume.
### Get a new role
Your resume, your career paths and your job matches refresh around the role you joined.
After the loop
## What happens after you get the job?
The loop does not stop at an offer. Tap I got the role and SkillDrift adds it to your resume, checks a month later that you started, counts each month in the role toward your skills, and helps you prepare for your review with a draft self-review built from your weekly wins.
It works for every goal, from your first internship to your next promotion. See how SkillDrift follows your career.
Why the loop matters
## One piece on its own goes stale. A loop compounds.
A course library tells you nothing about the role you want. A job board tells you nothing about why you were passed over. Joining them is the product.
### What a loop gives you
- A score that moves, measured against the role you actually want
- Learning chosen by your gap report, not by a catalogue
- Certificates written back into the resume the moment you finish
- Re-scoring after you upskill, free, every single time
### What one piece gives you
- A course you finish and forget to add anywhere
- A resume that formats what you already wrote
- A job board that ranks by recency, not by fit
- No way to tell whether any of it worked
Start free

# Entry Level Jobs and Internships, Scored for You | SkillDrift
URL: https://www.skilldrift.ai/jobs
Summary: Entry level jobs, fresher jobs, internships and jobs at every level, scored out of 100 against your resume. Only jobs with a trusted apply link, and closed jobs are never charged. Upload your resume free.

- SkillDrift
- Jobs
Jobs & internships
## Entry level jobs, internships and jobs at every level, scored out of 100 for you.
Jobs at every level, fresher roles and internships, each scored out of 100 against what your resume shows. SkillDrift only shows jobs with a trusted apply link, checks that a job is still open before you apply, and never charges for a job that has closed. Shortlist a job and it moves across your job board, so every application is tracked in one place.
See my matches - free How matching works

### Help asking for a referral
Who usually decides on the role, the recruiter, and someone doing the job now, with searches you run in your own LinkedIn. A connection note of up to 180 characters: your first one is free, then 15 credits. SkillDrift never contacts anyone for you.
Jobs you can act on

Only jobs you can actually apply to, chosen by the goal you picked.
### Trusted apply links only
A job shows only when it links to a main job board, an applicant system or the employer's own site. Copies on suspicious sites are hidden.
### Checked before you apply
Before the Apply Kit opens, SkillDrift checks the job page. If the job has closed, it tells you.
### Your goal decides
Looking for an internship puts internships first. Looking for your first full-time job shows full-time roles only.

### ATS parsing comes with it
Structure and formatting are fixed at the same time, so the resume reads correctly to a machine and still reads well to a person.

The rating
## Your ATS score, rated and not numbered
Every applicant tracking system parses a resume differently, so a single number out of 100 implies a precision no tool actually has. SkillDrift rates your resume across four bands, so the answer means the same thing whichever system reads it.
### Needs work
Structure or formatting is getting in the way. Parsers are likely to drop or mangle sections.
### Good
Readable by most systems, with specific things still costing you against your target role.
### Very good
Performs well with most ATS systems. What is left is content, not formatting.
### Excellent
Parses cleanly and reads strongly against the role you are aiming at.

- 03
### Fix what is named, then check again
An ATS rating tells you the machine can read you. It does not tell you that you are ready. The same upload also scores the gap between your skills and the role you want, and the loop that closes it starts from there.

# What Is Closed Loop Career Development? | SkillDrift
URL: https://www.skilldrift.ai/closed-loop-career-development
Summary: Closed loop career development measures your skill gap, closes it with learning built around your gap, and updates your resume and job matches as you go.

- SkillDrift
- How it works
- Closed loop career development
The category
## What is closed loop career development?
Closed loop career development measures the gap between a person and the role they want, closes it with learning built around that gap and that role, and updates their resume, gaps and job matches as they go. Closed means the end of one step feeds the start of the next. Finishing a course changes something you can see.
See your gaps How the loop works
Why it needs a name
## Parts of this loop already exist.
Most of the pieces are familiar. Each tool does its part and hands the person the job of joining them up.
Job boards
### Match you to roles
A score against today's resume. Nothing changes it except you rewriting the resume.
Course platforms
### Teach from a catalogue
The same course, written for everyone who picks it. Finishing it updates nothing else.
Company learning
### Personalise for employees
Useful inside one employer. It does not follow a person's own career or the open job market.
Chatbots
### Know only what you tell them
A study plan in a minute, and some now remember you. They cannot score you against real job postings or update your resume when you learn.
What is missing is the connection. A closed loop does the joining: the gap decides the learning, the learning is built around the learner’s gap, and finishing it changes the resume and the jobs they match without anyone editing anything.
How the loop works
## Five steps, and the second one is new.
Tailoring learning to one person’s gap and role used to cost too much. Generative AI changed that. SkillDrift uses it for one job: matching the learning to the gap your resume shows, for the role you want.
1
### Measure the gap
Against the role you want, from your resume, a job description or a mock interview.
2
### Build the learning
Built around your gap and your target role, not picked by topic.
3
### Prove it
Finish a short sprint and earn the certificate for it.
4
### Update everything
The certificate goes on your resume, your gaps shrink and jobs are rescored out of 100.
5
### Measure again
The next gap is visible instead of guessed at. The loop starts again.
Hyper-personalised learning
## The same subject, framed for the person reading it.
Hyper-personalised learning is built around one person’s measured gap and framed in the language of the role they want. The lesson itself changes, not only the order of recommendations.
A catalogue course
### Design systems
Written once, for designers and engineers. Every learner who picks it reads the same opening.
Recommended to you. Written for everyone.
A SkillDrift track, for a senior sales leader
### Design Systems at Scale
“As a senior sales leader, your advantage is that you can connect design-system decisions directly to revenue outcomes.”
Built around one person’s gap and target role. Quoted from a live SkillDrift track.
Check any learning product
## Four tests for hyper-personalised learning.
The first two tests make learning personal. The fourth makes it closed loop.
Test 1
Does it start from a gap that was measured, against a named role or a real posting, rather than a topic you chose?
Test 2
Is it framed for that role? The same subject should read differently for a sales leader and for a software engineer.
Test 3
Is it small enough to finish? One named gap at a time, in short sprints.
Test 4
Does finishing it move something you can see: your resume, your remaining gaps, the jobs you match?
The loop, closed
## Same job. Same person. Two gaps closed.
An example of what step 4 looks like. The job did not change. The resume did, without anyone editing it.
Data Analyst, entry level
58 / 100
Stretch
Excel SQL, missing Statistics, missing
→
two sprints, built for this gap
Data Analyst, entry level
81 / 100
Good fit
Excel SQL Statistics
After the job
## Does the loop stop when you get the job?
No. Tap I got the role and the new role goes onto your resume. Each month in it adds to the skills it uses, a logged win can go onto your resume, and before your review you get a draft self-review. The same scores keep moving towards the next role. See how SkillDrift follows your career.
FAQ
## Questions people ask about the loop.
For the full loop, end to end, see how it works.
What is closed loop career development?
Closed loop career development measures the gap between a person and the role they want, closes it with learning built around that gap and that role, and updates their resume, gaps and job matches as they go. Closed means the end of one step feeds the start of the next, so finishing a course changes something you can see.
What is hyper-personalised learning?
Hyper-personalised learning is learning built around one person's measured gap between their current skills and a specific role, and framed in the language of that role. It starts from what you are missing, not from a topic you picked, so what you learn next depends on your own gaps.
How is this different from an online course platform?
A course platform starts from its library: you choose a topic and take the same course as everyone else who chose it. SkillDrift starts from you. Each roadmap is built from your own gaps and matched to the role you are aiming at, and when you finish it your resume, your remaining gaps and your job match scores update.
Is there an AI that tells me which skills I am missing and helps me learn them?
Yes. That is what closed loop career development does. SkillDrift reads your resume against the role you want, names the skills you are missing, builds the learning around each gap, and rescores your job matches out of 100 as you close them.
What should I learn next for my career?
Start from the role you want, not from a topic. Compare your resume with a real job posting for that role, then learn the skill the posting asks for that your resume shows least. SkillDrift does this for you and updates the answer each time you finish something.
Where does the loop start?
With your resume. Upload it and SkillDrift names your gaps against the role you want, or against any job description you paste. A mock interview for the same role finds the gaps a resume cannot show, and those become learning too. The gap analysis is free.
Does the loop stop when you get the job?
No. The new role goes onto your resume, each month in it adds to the skills it uses, a logged win can go onto your resume, and before your review SkillDrift drafts a self-review. The same scores keep moving towards the next role.
## Start the loop with your resume.
See your gaps against the role you want, then start the first lesson built for your gap.
See your gaps

# Does SkillDrift work? The evidence, and its limits | SkillDrift
URL: https://www.skilldrift.ai/proof
Summary: Every outcome number SkillDrift publishes, what each one counts, and what it does not prove. Company reported, method stated, none of it independently audited.

- SkillDrift
- Proof
Proof
## Does SkillDrift actually work, and how would you know?
SkillDrift publishes five outcome numbers. All five are company reported, measured from our own product data, and none of them has been independently audited. This page sets out what SkillDrift can demonstrate from its own product data, what it deliberately does not measure, and what would be needed to prove more. The short version: we can show that readiness scores move as people learn, and that resumes and certificates update automatically when they do. We cannot yet show that a higher SkillDrift score causes a job offer, and we do not claim it.
Get my score - free See how it works
What is measured
## What can SkillDrift actually prove today?
Three things, all of them measured inside the product rather than reported by users. First, that a readiness score changes over time for people who complete learning, because the score is recomputed from the same resume every time it is read. Second, that a completed course writes a certificate into the resume without the user doing anything, because that write is the product mechanic rather than a manual step. Third, that a job match score out of 100 moves when the underlying skills change, because the match is recomputed against the same job description.
All three are statements about the machinery. None of them is a statement about employment.
What is counted
## What does SkillDrift count as a result, and what does it deliberately not count?
We count things the product does: a readiness score recomputed, a named gap closed, a certificate written into a resume, a tailored version generated, a job match re-scored. We do not count applications sent, interviews attended, offers received or salary changes, because we do not observe any of them.
A user can be hired the week after they close a gap and we would never know, and a user can close every gap and not get hired. Anyone claiming a career platform has measured your employment outcome is either integrated with your employer or guessing.
The limitation
## Is any of this independently verified?
No. Every number on this page is measured by SkillDrift from SkillDrift’s own data, and none of it has been audited by a third party. That is a real limitation and it applies to every AI career product currently on the market, ours included.
The reason to state it rather than bury it is that a score you cannot interrogate is worth less than a score you can: our numbers are worth exactly as much as the method behind them, which is why the method is on this page.
What would change it
## What would actually prove it, and what would have to be true?
Outcome validation needs three things we do not have yet: a large enough cohort followed for long enough, a control group of comparable people not using the product, and a reliable signal of what happened to them afterwards. The honest position is that none of the three exists today.
What we can do in the meantime is publish the method for every number we quote, correct anything found wrong, and never present a company reported figure as an independent one.
## See where you actually stand, before you take our word for anything.
No account needed to see your first score. Two minutes, one upload.
Get my score, free.
No card required · first application free · takes 2 minutes

# Compare SkillDrift with ChatGPT, LinkedIn Premium, Jobright and Internshala | SkillDrift
URL: https://www.skilldrift.ai/compare
Summary: Side by side comparisons of SkillDrift with ChatGPT, LinkedIn Premium, Jobright and Internshala, checked on 21 October 2026.

- SkillDrift
- Compare

# About SkillDrift - the end-to-end career platform
URL: https://www.skilldrift.ai/about
Summary: SkillDrift closes the loop between the job you want and the skills you have: score the gap, close it, and let your resume update itself as you go.

- SkillDrift
- About
About us
## About SkillDrift
SkillDrift closes the loop between the job you want and the skills you have: score the gap, close it, and let your resume update itself as you go.
Upload your resume - free See how it works
Why we built it
## Career advice is everywhere. Career measurement is not.
Most people looking for work are not short of advice. They are short of a number: some honest measure of the distance between where they are and the role they want, and a sense of which move closes the most of it.
Every tool in this market hands you one arc of the circle. A course library that knows nothing about the job you want. A resume builder that formats what you already wrote. A job board that ranks by recency rather than fit. Each is useful; none of them tells you whether anything is working.
SkillDrift exists to join them. Upload a resume, and the gap between you and a target role is scored out of 100. The roadmap that closes it is built from that score. Finish a sprint and the certificate writes itself back into the resume, the score re-scores itself free, and better roles unlock. Then it goes round again.
What we do differently
## What does SkillDrift do that a chatbot or a job board does not?
Most tools hand you one piece and forget you. SkillDrift keeps one record of you, so every step counts.
### It remembers every step
Courses you finish, interviews you practise and months in a role all move the same scores.
### Jobs you can act on
Jobs and internships scored out of 100, only with a trusted apply link, and never charged once closed.
### Honest about the gap
Every missing skill is named, and an interview can tell you an answer would not have got you through.
### It stays after the offer
Your new role, your weekly wins, your review and your next move, in the same place.
### Works where you are
Jobs and internships in the US, India and worldwide, with prices in your currency.
How we operate
## Three commitments we hold ourselves to.
### We never invent your numbers
Every figure on your resume is one you supplied. The rewrite asks you what happened and writes from your answers, so nothing can surprise you in an interview.
### Diagnosis stays free
Finding out where you stand should not be behind a card. Skill gaps, your career path, job matching and re-scoring are free permanently.
### Your resume is yours
We store it so you never upload twice, delete abandoned anonymous uploads after 30 days, and never email you off the back of a file you dropped to get a score.

# Accountant Skills: What the Job Asks For in 2026 | SkillDrift
URL: https://www.skilldrift.ai/skills/accountant
Summary: The skills an accountant needs in 2026, from reconciliations to reporting and accounting software, which ones decide the offer, and how to check your own gap.

- SkillDrift
- Skills by role
- Accountant
## Accountant skills in 2026
An accountant needs a firm grasp of accounting standards, bookkeeping and reconciliations, financial reporting, tax and compliance, and confident use of accounting software and Excel. As more routine work is automated, employers put more weight on analysis, accuracy and explaining the numbers to people outside finance.
Check yours against a real accountant job. Most accountant resumes list duties such as the month end close. The offer usually turns on whether the resume shows the accuracy, speed or saving that came from doing them well.
## Start with your resume.
Takes about a minute
Upload it once. You get your readiness score, your closest roles, your real gaps and week one of a plan built for them.
Drop your resume here
PDF, DOC or DOCX · up to 5 MB · takes about a minute
Get my readiness score
We read your resume to score it and find matches. We store it so you don’t have to upload it again if you make an account, and delete it after 30 days if you don’t. Privacy policy.
Don’t have a resume? Build one with SkillDrift AI in 2 minutes. Build my resume
Technical skills
## Accounting skills most postings ask for
### Accounting standards
IFRS, US GAAP or the local standard, and applying them to real transactions.
### Bookkeeping and reconciliations
Ledgers, bank and account reconciliations, and clearing differences before month end.
### Financial reporting
Preparing statements and management reports that stand up to review.
### Tax and compliance
Returns, indirect taxes and the filing calendar for the country you work in.
### Accounting software and Excel
QuickBooks, Xero, SAP, Oracle or Tally, plus lookups, pivot tables and clean models in Excel.
Human skills
## Human skills that decide the job
### Attention to detail
Finding the error before an auditor does.
### Integrity
Saying no to a number that is not right, even under pressure.
### Explaining numbers
Telling a manager what the figures mean in plain language.
### Deadline discipline
Closing the month on time, every month.
What decides the offer
## The skills that decide the offer
Most people who reach the interview have the core list. These are the skills that usually separate them.
### Analysis, not only processing
Software now handles much of the data entry. Interviewers look for accountants who can explain why a number moved and what to do about it.
### Improving the process
A candidate who shortened the close or automated a reconciliation shows more than one who only ran it.
### Clear communication
In the SkillDrift Jobs Index, communication is among the most requested skills across all postings. For an accountant it means reports and explanations that people outside finance can follow.
On your resume
## How to show these skills on your resume
The second line shows the software, the scope, a process improvement and a result. A screening system matches words, so a skill that is not written down is a skill that does not count.
### Before
Responsible for month end closing and reconciliations.
### After
Ran the month end close for three entities in Xero, and cut it from eight working days to five by automating the bank reconciliations.
See how a screening system reads your resume with the ATS score checker, then turn the gaps into a plan with a career roadmap.
[Image: A real internship scored 75 out of 100 in SkillDrift, with the five skills the person already has and the three to close]
What you see after the upload: each accountant job scored out of 100, the skills you already show, and the ones to close, each with a roadmap.
### Why check this in SkillDrift?
- Real accountant jobs, scored for you Each one scored out of 100 against your resume, with the skills you already show and the ones to close named.
- A plan that moves your scores Learning built for each gap and sized to your hours. Finish it and the certificate goes into your resume, and the jobs that ask for that skill move up.
- Ready for the interview Practise the accountant interview out loud and get an honest score out of 10, with the weak answers turned into a plan.
By title
## Staff accountant, accountant and senior accountant skills
A junior or staff accountant role leans on bookkeeping, reconciliations and accuracy. An accountant role adds reporting, tax and more of the close. A senior accountant or finance manager role adds review, analysis, audits and guiding junior staff. The step up is usually decided by analysis and by explaining the numbers, not by processing more of them.
FAQ
## Questions people ask
What skills does an accountant need?
Accounting standards, bookkeeping and reconciliations, financial reporting, tax and compliance, accounting software and Excel, and attention to detail.
What accounting skills should I put on my resume?
Name the standards, the software and the processes you ran, then show one result such as a faster close or a clean audit.
Will automation replace accountants?
Automation is taking over much of the routine data entry. The work that remains is analysis, judgment and explaining the numbers, and that is where an accountant can show the most value.
How do I check my skills against an accountant job?
Upload your resume to SkillDrift and pick the job. It names the skills the posting asks for that your resume does not show, scores the job out of 100, and builds a learning path for each gap.

# Administrative Assistant Skills: What the Job Asks For in 2026 | SkillDrift
URL: https://www.skilldrift.ai/skills/administrative-assistant
Summary: The skills an administrative assistant needs in 2026, from scheduling and office software to record keeping, which ones decide the offer, and how to check your own gap.

- SkillDrift
- Skills by role
- Administrative Assistant
## Administrative assistant skills in 2026
An administrative assistant needs confident use of Microsoft Office or Google Workspace, scheduling and calendar management, clear written communication, accurate record keeping and strong organisation. Employers also look for discretion with confidential information, and the judgment to handle several requests at once in the right order.
Check yours against a real administrative assistant job. Most administrative resumes describe the role as general office support. A hiring manager looks for the specific calendars, records and systems the candidate kept running.

Technical skills
## Office skills most postings ask for
### Microsoft Office or Google Workspace
Word or Docs for letters and reports, Excel or Sheets for lists and simple tracking, and Outlook or Gmail for email.
### Scheduling and calendar management
Booking meetings across several calendars and time zones, and handling changes without double booking.
### Record keeping
Filing documents, invoices and contacts so that anyone on the team can find them.
### Travel and event arrangements
Booking travel, rooms and catering within budget and company policy.
### Data entry and basic bookkeeping
Entering data accurately, tracking expenses and preparing simple reports.
### Collaboration tools
Shared drives, video calls, and tools such as Teams, Slack or a CRM.
Human skills
## Human skills that decide the job
### Written communication
Clear, polite emails and messages on behalf of a manager or a team.
### Organisation
Keeping track of many small tasks and deadlines at once.
### Discretion
Handling confidential information, such as salaries or personal records, with care.
### Prioritisation
Deciding which request to deal with first when several arrive at the same time.
What decides the offer
## The skills that decide the offer
Most people who reach the interview have the core list. These are the skills that usually separate them.
### Handling competing requests
Interviewers often ask what you did when two managers needed something at the same time. A clear account of how you decided, and how you told both people, carries a lot of weight.
### Accuracy
A wrong meeting time or a misfiled invoice causes problems later. Candidates who can describe how they check their own work stand out.
### Learning new tools
Offices change their software often. Employers value assistants who learn a new system quickly, including AI tools for drafting and note taking, and who help others use it.
On your resume
## How to show these skills on your resume
The second line shows the software, the scope, record keeping and a process improvement. A screening system matches words, so a skill that is not written down is a skill that does not count.
### Before
Provided administrative support to the management team.
### After
Managed calendars and travel for four senior managers in Outlook, kept the contracts register current in SharePoint, and set up a shared request tracker that reduced repeat questions to the team.

By title
## Administrative assistant, executive assistant and office manager skills
An administrative assistant role supports a team with scheduling, records and correspondence. An executive assistant role supports one or two senior leaders closely, and adds managing their priorities, preparing meeting papers and handling sensitive matters. An office manager role adds suppliers, budgets, facilities and sometimes a small team. The step up is usually decided by judgment and by owning outcomes, such as an office move or an event that ran to plan.
FAQ

What skills does an administrative assistant need?
Microsoft Office or Google Workspace, scheduling and calendar management, written communication, record keeping, organisation, prioritisation and discretion.
What should I put under skills on an administrative assistant resume?
Name the software you use, the calendars and records you manage, and one process you improved. Add organisation and discretion, each backed by a line in your experience.
What is the difference between an administrative assistant and an executive assistant?
An administrative assistant usually supports a team. An executive assistant usually supports one or two senior leaders and handles more of their priorities and confidential work.

## Business analyst skills in 2026
A business analyst needs to gather and write clear requirements, map how a process works today and how it should work, analyse data with SQL and spreadsheets, and turn all of it into a recommendation people can act on. Most roles also expect a working knowledge of agile delivery and the tools teams use to track it.

Technical skills
## Analysis skills most postings ask for
### Requirements gathering
Running workshops and interviews, then writing requirements and user stories a team can build from.
### Process mapping
Drawing how work flows today and where it breaks, with BPMN or simple flowcharts.
### SQL and spreadsheets
Pulling and checking the data yourself instead of waiting for someone else.
### Data visualisation
Power BI, Tableau or similar, and one chart that answers one question.

Human skills

### Asking the right questions
Finding the real problem behind the request.
### Clear writing
Documents that a developer and a director can both follow.

Agreeing what is in scope, and what is not, before work starts.
What decides the offer
## The skills that decide the offer
Most people who reach the interview have the core list. These are the skills that usually separate them.
### From analysis to recommendation
Employers want analysts who say what to do next. Show one piece of work that changed a decision, a process or a cost.
### Handling conflicting stakeholders
Interviewers often ask about two people who wanted different things. A clear account of how you reached agreement carries a lot of weight.
### Hands on data
Many business analyst roles now expect SQL. Being able to check a number yourself sets a candidate apart.

## Business analyst, data analyst or product manager?
The three roles overlap. A business analyst works out what a process or system needs and writes it down for the people who build it. A data analyst answers questions with data. FAQ

What skills are needed for a business analyst?
Requirements gathering, process mapping, SQL and spreadsheets, a visualisation tool, agile delivery, stakeholder management and clear writing.
Does a business analyst need technical skills?

What is the difference between a business analyst and a data analyst?
A business analyst focuses on processes, requirements and change. A data analyst focuses on answering questions with data. Many roles blend the two.

# Customer Service Skills: What the Job Asks For in 2026 | SkillDrift
URL: https://www.skilldrift.ai/skills/customer-service

- SkillDrift
- Skills by role
- Customer Service
## Customer service skills in 2026
Customer service roles ask for clear communication in speech and in writing, active listening, patient problem solving, product knowledge and confident use of a ticketing or CRM system. More roles now add live chat, several channels in one shift and working alongside AI assistants. Underneath all of it sits empathy: understanding what the customer actually needs, then solving it.
Check yours against a real customer service job. Almost every customer service resume says excellent communication skills. So does every other resume, which is why the line tells a hiring manager nothing about how you handle a difficult customer.

Takes about a minute

Technical skills
## Service skills most postings ask for
### Ticketing and CRM systems
Zendesk, Freshdesk, Salesforce or similar. Logging every case so the next person can pick it up.
### Multichannel support
Phone, email, live chat and social messages, often in the same shift.
### Product knowledge
Knowing the product well enough to answer without escalating.
### Troubleshooting
Finding the cause of a problem step by step, not only the symptom.
### Service metrics
Knowing what first contact resolution, handling time and satisfaction scores measure, and how your work moves them.
Human skills
## Human skills that decide the conversation
### Active listening
Hearing the real problem before offering an answer.
### Empathy
Showing the customer you understand, without promising what you cannot deliver.
### Calm under pressure
Handling an angry customer, then taking the next call as if it were the first.
### Clear writing
Chat and email replies that solve the problem in one message.
What decides the offer
## The skills that decide the offer
Most people who reach the interview have the core list. These are the skills that usually separate them.
### Calming a difficult customer
Interviews often include a role play with an upset customer. Candidates who acknowledge the problem, ask one clear question and give a next step tend to do well. Candidates who argue or over promise tend not to.
### Solving it the first time
Employers track how often a problem is solved in the first contact. A candidate who can explain how they raised that rate, or kept it high, stands out.
### Written communication
In the SkillDrift Jobs Index, communication is among the most requested skills across all postings. In customer service much of it is written, in chat and email.
On your resume
## How to show these skills on your resume
The same job, but the second line shows the system, the channels, a service metric and problem solving. A screening system matches words, so a skill that is not written down is a skill that does not count.
### Before
Handled customer queries and complaints.
### After
Resolved chat and email cases in Zendesk, kept satisfaction scores above the team target, and rewrote the three saved replies that caused the most follow up questions.

By title
## Customer service representative, associate and manager skills
A customer service associate or representative role leans on product knowledge, the ticketing system and a high volume of conversations. A senior or specialist role adds complex cases, escalations and training new joiners. A customer service manager role adds coaching, scheduling, quality reviews and reporting on service metrics. The step from agent to manager is usually decided by coaching and by reading the numbers, not by handling more calls.
FAQ
## Questions people ask
What skills do you need for customer service?
Clear spoken and written communication, active listening, empathy, product knowledge, troubleshooting, a ticketing or CRM system, and staying calm under pressure.
What should I put under skills on a customer service resume?
Name the system you used, the channels you covered and one service metric you moved. Then add two or three human skills, each backed by a line in your experience.
What skills does a customer service manager need?
Coaching, scheduling, quality review, handling escalations, and reporting on metrics such as satisfaction scores and first contact resolution.

# Data Engineer Skills: What the Job Asks For in 2026 | SkillDrift
URL: https://www.skilldrift.ai/skills/data-engineer
Summary: The skills a data engineer needs in 2026, from SQL and Python to pipelines, Spark and cloud platforms, which ones decide the offer, and how to check your own gap.

- SkillDrift
- Skills by role
- Data Engineer
## Data engineer skills in 2026
A data engineer needs SQL and Python used to a professional standard, the ability to build and run ETL and data pipelines, a distributed processing tool such as Apache Spark, one cloud data platform, data modelling, and an orchestration tool to schedule and monitor the work. Around those sit the human skills of clear communication with the analysts and data scientists who use the data, and ownership when a pipeline fails.
Check yours against a real data engineer job. Most data engineering resumes list tools. The offer usually turns on whether the resume shows data that arrived on time, stayed correct and was used by someone.
## Start with your resume.
Takes about a minute
Upload it once. You get your readiness score, your closest roles, your real gaps and week one of a plan built for them.
Drop your resume here
PDF, DOC or DOCX · up to 5 MB · takes about a minute
Get my readiness score
We read your resume to score it and find matches. We store it so you don’t have to upload it again if you make an account, and delete it after 30 days if you don’t. Privacy policy.
Don’t have a resume? Build one with SkillDrift AI in 2 minutes. Build my resume
Technical skills
## Technical skills most postings ask for
### SQL
Complex joins, window functions and query tuning on large tables.
### Python
Pipeline code that is tested, readable and safe to run again.
### ETL and data pipelines
Moving data from source systems into a warehouse or lake, in batches or as a stream, and handling late or bad records.
### Apache Spark
Processing data too large for one machine, and knowing how partitions and joins affect speed and cost.
### Cloud data platforms
One of AWS, Azure or Google Cloud, plus a warehouse such as Snowflake, BigQuery, Redshift or Databricks.
### Data modelling
Designing tables and schemas, such as a star schema, that analysts can query without help.
### Orchestration
Airflow, Dagster or a similar tool to schedule jobs, manage dependencies and retry failures.
### Data quality and testing
Checks that catch missing, duplicated or wrong data before anyone reports on it.
Human skills
## Human skills that decide the job
### Communication
Agreeing with analysts and data scientists what the data means and when it will arrive.
### Ownership
Fixing a failed pipeline quickly and writing down what caused it.
### Attention to detail
Noticing when a number looks wrong before it reaches a report.
What decides the offer
## The skills that decide the offer
Most people who reach the interview have the core list. These are the skills that usually separate them.
### Reliability you can show
Interviewers often ask about a pipeline that broke. A clear account of how you found the cause, fixed it and stopped it from happening again carries a lot of weight.
### Data modelling
Many interviews include a design exercise. Candidates who ask how the data will be used before they draw any tables tend to do well.
### Cost and performance
Cloud processing is billed by use. Employers value engineers who can make a slow or expensive job faster and cheaper, and explain how they did it.
On your resume
## How to show these skills on your resume
The second line shows the tools, the platform, data quality and a result. Use your own real numbers. A screening system matches words, so a skill that is not written down is a skill that does not count.
### Before
Built ETL pipelines using Spark and Airflow.
### After
Built and ran Spark pipelines in Airflow that load sales data into Snowflake each morning, added data quality checks, and halved the nightly run time.

By title
## Data engineer, data analyst or data scientist?
A data engineer builds and runs the systems that collect, clean and store data. A data analyst uses that data to answer business questions. A data scientist builds models that predict or classify. An analytics engineer works between engineering and analysis, and focuses on data modelling inside the warehouse. Many roles blend two of these, so read the posting to see which mix the employer wants.
FAQ
## Questions people ask
What skills are needed for a data engineer?
SQL, Python, ETL and data pipelines, Apache Spark, a cloud data platform, data modelling, an orchestration tool such as Airflow, data quality checks, and clear communication with the people who use the data.
Does a data engineer need to know Python?
Most roles expect Python, and some accept Scala or Java. SQL is expected in nearly every data engineering role.
What skills does a data engineer need for a first job?
SQL and Python used well, one cloud platform, and one project that moves data from a source into a database on a schedule. Show that the project ran more than once and that you checked the data it produced.

# Data Scientist Skills: What the Job Asks For in 2026 | SkillDrift
URL: https://www.skilldrift.ai/skills/data-scientist
Summary: The skills needed for a data scientist in 2026, from Python and statistics to machine learning, which ones decide the offer, and how to check your own gap.

- SkillDrift
- Skills by role
- Data Scientist
## Data scientist skills in 2026
A data scientist needs Python and SQL used to a professional standard, a firm grounding in statistics, machine learning from building a model to judging whether it works, and the ability to explain a result to the people who will act on it. Some roles now add work with large language models and putting models into production.
Check yours against a real data scientist job. Most data science resumes list libraries and models. The offer usually turns on whether the resume shows a model that was used, and what changed because of it.
## Start with your resume.
Takes about a minute
Upload it once. You get your readiness score, your closest roles, your real gaps and week one of a plan built for them.
Drop your resume here
PDF, DOC or DOCX · up to 5 MB · takes about a minute

Technical skills
## Technical skills most postings ask for
### Python
pandas, NumPy and scikit-learn at least. In the SkillDrift Jobs Index, Python passed communication in September 2026 as the most requested skill across all job postings.
### SQL
Getting your own data from real tables, joins and window functions included.
### Statistics and experiments
Distributions, hypothesis tests, and designing an A/B test that answers the question.
### Machine learning
Choosing a model, validating it honestly and knowing when a simple one is enough.
### Deployment
Getting a model out of a notebook: version control, cloud, and monitoring after launch.
Human skills
## Human skills that decide the job
### Framing the problem
Turning a vague business question into one that data can answer.
### Communication
Explaining what a model does, and does not do, to someone who is not a data scientist.
### Business judgment
Knowing which result is worth acting on.
### Curiosity
Checking the data that looks wrong before it reaches a decision.
What decides the offer
## The skills that decide the offer
Most people who reach the interview have the core list. These are the skills that usually separate them.
### Impact, not accuracy
Interviewers ask what happened after the model. A small model that changed a decision beats a complex one that never left the notebook.
### Statistics under questioning
Many interviews test statistics directly. Be ready to explain why a result is real, not only that it is significant.
### Explaining the result
In the SkillDrift Jobs Index, communication is still among the most requested skills across all postings. For a data scientist it decides whether the model gets used.
On your resume
## How to show these skills on your resume
The second line shows Python, the data, the model and a business result. A screening system matches words, so a skill that is not written down is a skill that does not count.
### Before
Built machine learning models in Python.
### After
Built a churn model in Python on two years of subscription data. The retention team used it to target offers, and kept more customers than with the previous rule based list.

By title
## Data scientist, data analyst or machine learning engineer?
A data analyst answers business questions with existing data. A data scientist builds models and predictions and tests whether they hold. A machine learning engineer puts models into production and keeps them running. Many roles blend two of the three, so read the posting rather than the title.
FAQ
## Questions people ask
What skills are needed for a data scientist?
Python, SQL, statistics, machine learning, some knowledge of deployment, and the ability to frame a problem and explain the result.
Is a postgraduate degree required to become a data scientist?
Many postings ask for one, and many also accept equivalent experience. A portfolio with one model that was used in practice often carries as much weight.
What is the difference between a data scientist and a data analyst?
A data analyst answers questions with existing data. A data scientist builds models that predict or classify. Many roles blend the two.

## Graphic designer skills in 2026
A graphic designer needs professional use of Adobe Illustrator, Photoshop and InDesign, and often Figma as well. They also need a strong command of typography, layout and colour, and the ability to work within a brand system and extend it. Employers expect a portfolio that shows the work and the thinking behind it, and the ability to take feedback and turn it into a better design.
Check yours against a real graphic designer job. Most graphic design resumes list software. Hiring managers look at the portfolio first, then read the resume for the brief, the audience and the result behind each piece.

Technical skills
## Design skills most postings ask for
### Adobe Illustrator
Logos, icons and illustrations built as clean vector files.
### Adobe Photoshop
Editing and combining images for print and for screens.
### Adobe InDesign
Multi page layouts such as brochures, reports and books, set up correctly for print.
### Figma
Designing for screens, building shared components and working with product teams.
### Typography and layout
Choosing and pairing typefaces, and arranging content on a grid so that the most important message is read first.
### Brand systems
Applying brand guidelines consistently, and extending them to new formats.
### Preparing files for production
Colour modes, bleed, resolution and export settings for print, web and social media.
Human skills
## Human skills that decide the job
### Taking feedback
Listening to comments, asking what problem each one points to, and revising the design with that in mind.
### Understanding the brief
Asking who the design is for and what it needs to achieve before starting.
### Presenting work
Explaining design choices in terms the client or the team cares about.
### Time management
Delivering several projects on deadline, with time left for revisions.
What decides the offer
## The skills that decide the offer
Most people who reach the interview have the core list. These are the skills that usually separate them.
### A focused portfolio
Hiring managers often look at the portfolio before the resume. A small set of strong projects, each with the brief and the result, tends to do better than a long gallery.
### Explaining design decisions
Interviews often include a portfolio review. Candidates who can say why they chose a layout or a typeface, and who it was for, stand out.
### Working with AI tools
Many teams now use AI tools for images and layouts. Employers want designers who can use them and still judge quality, accuracy and fit with the brand.

Designed a new event identity in Illustrator and InDesign, built templates the marketing team reused for a year of campaigns, and prepared all print and social files to the brand guidelines.

## HR skills in 2026
An HR professional needs employment law and policy knowledge, recruitment and onboarding, employee relations, HR systems and data, and the human skills of confidentiality, judgment and clear communication. An HR manager adds workforce planning, performance management and advising leaders.
Check yours against a real HR professional job. HR resumes often list duties rather than outcomes. The skills are there, but a screening system and a hiring manager cannot see them.

Technical skills
## HR skills most postings ask for
### Employment law and policy
Knowing the rules where you work and turning them into clear policy.
### Recruitment and onboarding
Running a hiring process end to end and getting new joiners productive.
### HR systems
Using an HRIS well, and keeping records accurate.
### People data
Reading attrition, hiring and engagement numbers, often in Excel or a dashboard.
### Performance management
Setting up reviews and helping managers run them fairly.
### Payroll and benefits basics
Understanding how pay and benefits work, even when another team runs them.
Human skills
## Human skills that HR roles depend on
### Employee relations
Handling grievances and difficult conversations calmly and fairly.
### Confidentiality and judgment
Knowing what to share, with whom, and when.
### Communication
Writing policy people understand and explaining decisions clearly.
### Stakeholder management
Advising managers and leaders who do not report to you.
What decides the offer
## The skills that decide the offer
Most people who reach the interview have the core list. These are the skills that usually separate them.
### People data
More HR postings ask for someone who can turn attrition or hiring numbers into a decision. Many HR professionals do this and never write it down.
### Advising leaders
Especially for HR manager roles, the question is whether you can change a leader’s mind with evidence and tact.
### Employee relations
Interviewers often ask for a difficult case. A clear, fair and confidential answer carries a lot of weight.
On your resume
## How to show these skills on your resume
The second line shows recruitment, onboarding design and a measured result. Use your own real numbers.
### Before
Responsible for recruitment and onboarding.
### After
Ran hiring for 40 roles a year across three teams and cut time to productivity for new joiners with a structured first month plan.

## HR executive, HR generalist and HR manager skills
An HR executive or generalist role is broad: recruitment, records, policy and employee questions. An HR manager role adds workforce planning, performance management, employee relations cases and advising senior leaders. FAQ
## Questions people ask
What are the most important HR skills?
Employment law and policy, recruitment and onboarding, employee relations, HR systems and people data, plus confidentiality, judgment and clear communication.
What HR skills should I put on my resume?
The ones the posting names, written as work you did with a result. Recruitment, onboarding, employee relations, HRIS and people data are the most common.
What skills does an HR manager need?
Everything an HR generalist does, plus workforce planning, performance management, handling complex cases and advising leaders.

## Marketing skills in 2026
Marketing roles ask for a mix of craft and numbers: writing and content, digital channels such as search, social and email, a working knowledge of analytics, and a clear understanding of the customer. Many roles now add marketing automation and AI tools for content and research. What ties them together is choosing the right audience and message, then measuring whether it worked.
Check yours against a real marketing job. Most marketing resumes list channels and tools. Few show a result, and a hiring manager reads the result first.

Technical skills
## Marketing skills most postings ask for
### Content and copywriting
Writing that makes one reader take one action, on any channel.
### SEO and search
How people search, how pages rank, and how paid search differs from organic.
### Social media and email
Planning, publishing and testing on the channels the audience actually uses.
### Analytics
Google Analytics or similar, attribution, and reading a dashboard without guessing.
### Marketing automation and CRM
HubSpot, Salesforce or similar. Segments, workflows and lead scoring.
Human skills
## Human skills that decide the campaign
### Customer understanding
Knowing who the buyer is, what they worry about and what they search for.
### Creativity with a brief
Fresh ideas that still answer the question the business asked.
### Clear writing
Briefs, plans and reports that other teams can act on.
### Working across teams
Getting sales, product and design to agree on one plan.
What decides the offer
## The skills that decide the offer
Most people who reach the interview have the core list. These are the skills that usually separate them.
### Proving results
Interviewers ask what changed because of your work. A campaign described by its reach loses to one described by the leads, signups or sales it produced.
### Testing and learning
Employers want marketers who run a test, read it honestly and change course. Show one test that did not work and what you did next.
### Using AI with judgment
Many teams now use AI tools for drafts and research. Interviewers want to know that you can use them and still judge what is good enough to publish.
On your resume

Managed social media accounts for the brand.

Planned and ran the brand Instagram and LinkedIn calendar, tested two new content formats a month, and grew inbound leads from social by a third in six months.

A marketing executive or associate role leans on running channels and content day to day. A digital marketing role puts more weight on search, paid media, analytics and automation. The step up is usually decided by owning a number, such as pipeline or revenue from marketing, rather than a list of activities.

Search, both organic and paid, social media, email, analytics and marketing automation, plus the ability to test a channel and report what it produced.

# Product Manager Skills: What the Role Requires in 2026 | SkillDrift

- SkillDrift
- Skills by role
- Product Manager
## Product manager skills in 2026
A product manager needs to understand users, decide what to build and in what order, work with engineering and design to ship it, and measure whether it worked. That takes discovery, prioritisation, clear writing, data skills and the ability to lead people who do not report to you.
Check yours against a real product manager job. Product management is hard to show on a resume because the work is shared. The skill is in the decisions, and those rarely make it onto the page.
## Start with your resume.
Takes about a minute
Upload it once. You get your readiness score, your closest roles, your real gaps and week one of a plan built for them.
Drop your resume here

Technical skills
## Product skills most postings ask for
### User research and discovery
Finding the real problem before building a solution.
### Prioritisation
Choosing what to build first, and explaining why.
### Roadmapping
Turning strategy into a plan the team can follow.
### Product analytics
Defining success metrics and reading the data, often with SQL or an analytics tool.
### Technical understanding
Enough to discuss trade offs with engineers, not to write the code.
### Working with AI features
Knowing what AI can and cannot do inside a product.
Human skills
## Human skills product roles depend on
### Written communication
Specs, decision notes and updates people actually read.
### Stakeholder management
Aligning leaders, sales, support and engineering.
### Leading without authority
Getting a team to commit when nobody reports to you.
What decides the offer
## The skills that decide the offer
Most people who reach the interview have the core list. These are the skills that usually separate them.
### Prioritisation you can explain
Interviewers often ask what you said no to, and why. A clear answer shows judgment more than any list of features.
### Measuring outcomes
Postings ask for product managers who define a metric before building and check it after. Show one example with a real number.
### Clear writing
Much of the job is written. A short, clear decision note is one of the strongest signals a candidate can give.
On your resume
## How to show these skills on your resume
The second line shows discovery, prioritisation and an outcome. Use your own real result.
### Before
Managed the mobile app roadmap.
### After
Owned the mobile app roadmap, cut three low value features after user interviews, and shipped a new onboarding flow that raised week one retention.

## Associate product manager or product manager?
An associate product manager role focuses on execution: writing specs, running a backlog and learning discovery. A product manager owns outcomes for an area. A senior product manager adds strategy and influence across teams. The skills are the same, the scope and the evidence grow.
FAQ
## Questions people ask
What skills are required for a product manager?
User research and discovery, prioritisation, roadmapping, product analytics, enough technical understanding to discuss trade offs, clear writing and stakeholder management.
Does a product manager need to code?
Usually no. They need to understand technical trade offs well enough to make good decisions with engineers.
What skills are needed for product management as a first role?
Clear writing, basic analytics, curiosity about users, and evidence of shipping something with others, even outside a product job.

# Skills Required for a Project Manager in 2026 | SkillDrift
URL: https://www.skilldrift.ai/skills/project-manager
Summary: The skills required for a project manager in 2026, from planning and risk to budgets and agile methods, which ones decide the offer, and how to check your own gap.

- SkillDrift
- Skills by role
- Project Manager
## Project manager skills in 2026
A project manager needs to plan and schedule work, manage risks and issues, control a budget, keep stakeholders informed and in agreement, and run the project with a suitable method, whether agile, waterfall or a mix of the two. Most roles also expect confident use of a project tool such as Jira, Asana or Microsoft Project, along with clear communication and the ability to lead a team.
Check yours against a real project manager job. Most project manager resumes list the projects delivered. The offer usually turns on whether the resume shows what was at risk, and how the project still finished on time and on budget.
## Start with your resume.
Takes about a minute
Upload it once. You get your readiness score, your closest roles, your real gaps and week one of a plan built for them.
Drop your resume here
PDF, DOC or DOCX · up to 5 MB · takes about a minute
Get my readiness score
We read your resume to score it and find matches. We store it so you don’t have to upload it again if you make an account, and delete it after 30 days if you don’t. Privacy policy.
Don’t have a resume? Build one with SkillDrift AI in 2 minutes. Build my resume
Technical skills
## Project skills most postings ask for
### Planning and scheduling
Breaking work into tasks, estimating it, and building a schedule with clear milestones and dependencies.
### Risk and issue management
Spotting what could go wrong early, keeping a risk log, and acting while there is still time.
### Budgeting and cost control
Building a project budget, tracking spend against it, and explaining any difference.
### Agile and waterfall methods
Scrum or Kanban for work that changes often, a staged plan for work with fixed requirements, and knowing which one fits the project.
### Project tools
Jira, Asana, Microsoft Project, Smartsheet or similar, kept current so that the plan matches the actual state of the work.
### Scope and change control
Agreeing what is in the project, and handling requests to change it through a clear process.
Human skills
## Human skills that decide the project
### Stakeholder management
Keeping sponsors, clients and teams informed and in agreement, especially when the news is bad.
### Communication
Status reports, meeting notes and decisions that people can act on.
### Leadership
Getting a team to commit to a plan, often when the team members do not report to you.
### Problem solving
Finding a workable option when a deadline, a budget or a resource changes.
What decides the offer
## The skills that decide the offer
Most people who reach the interview have the core list. These are the skills that usually separate them.
### Recovering a project
Interviewers often ask about a project that went off track. A clear account of what you noticed, what you changed and how the project finished carries a lot of weight.
### Raising problems early
Sponsors value project managers who raise a risk while there is still time to act. Show one example where an early warning changed the outcome.
### Choosing the method
Employers want project managers who can explain why a project used agile, waterfall or a mix. A reason based on the work itself is a strong answer.
On your resume
## How to show these skills on your resume
The second line shows scope, risk management, recovery and budget control. Use your own real figures. A screening system matches words, so a skill that is not written down is a skill that does not count.
### Before
Managed IT projects from start to finish.
### After
Led a 12 month system migration for three departments, kept a weekly risk log, brought a delayed data transfer back on schedule, and delivered within the agreed budget.

By title
## Project coordinator, project manager and program manager skills
A project coordinator role supports the plan by scheduling meetings, tracking tasks and keeping documents current. A project manager role owns the plan, the budget, the risks and the result. A program manager role oversees several related projects, and adds tracking of benefits and managing senior stakeholders. A recognised project management certification helps in many postings, and evidence of projects delivered usually carries the most weight.
FAQ
## Questions people ask
What skills are required for a project manager?
Planning and scheduling, risk management, budgeting, scope control, agile and waterfall methods, a project tool, stakeholder management, communication and leadership.
Do I need a certification to become a project manager?
Many postings list a project management certification as preferred, and some require one. Evidence that you delivered real projects usually matters more, and a certification is strongest when it comes with that evidence.
What skills does a first time project manager need?
Organisation, clear communication, a working knowledge of one project tool, and evidence of coordinating work with others, even outside a formal project role.
How do I check my skills against a project manager job?
Upload your resume to SkillDrift and pick the job. It names the skills the posting asks for that your resume does not show, scores the job out of 100, and builds a learning path for each gap.

Keeping records current so the team can trust the numbers.
### Forecasting
Saying what will close this month, and being right.
### Negotiation and closing
Agreeing terms that both sides will keep.
Human skills
## Human skills that decide deals
### Discovery
Asking questions that get to the actual problem, then listening.
### Objection handling
Treating an objection as information rather than a rejection.
### Written follow up
Emails and proposals a buyer can forward to their own manager.
### Resilience
Recovering from a lost deal the same afternoon.
What decides the offer
## The skills that decide the offer
Most people who reach the interview have the core list. These are the skills that usually separate them.
### Discovery
Interviews often include a short role play. Candidates who pitch in the first minute tend to lose. Candidates who ask three good questions first tend to win.
### Forecast honesty
A manager who has been let down by optimistic pipelines wants to hear how you decided what would close, and what you did when a deal slipped.
### Written communication
In the SkillDrift Jobs Index, communication is still one of the most requested skills across postings. In sales a large part of it is written.
On your resume
## How to show these skills on your resume
The first line shows closing. The second shows prospecting, pipeline building and closing, with the same result.
### Before
Achieved 120 percent of annual quota.
### After
Built a new mid market territory from zero to a full pipeline in two quarters, then reached 120 percent of quota.

By title
## Sales associate, sales executive and sales manager skills
A sales associate role leans on product knowledge, customer service and a high volume of conversations. A sales executive role covers the full cycle with a personal target. A sales manager role adds coaching, hiring, territory planning and team forecasting. Coaching is the skill that most often separates a strong seller from a strong manager.
FAQ
## Questions people ask
What skills does a sales executive need?
Prospecting, qualification, discovery, objection handling, negotiation and closing, CRM and pipeline management, forecasting, and clear written follow up.
What are the most important sales associate skills?
Product knowledge, customer service, handling many conversations well, and basic CRM use.
What skills does a sales manager need that a sales executive does not?
Coaching, hiring, territory planning and forecasting for a whole team.
