# Skills Needed for a Software Engineer in 2026 | SkillDrift
URL: https://www.skilldrift.ai/skills/software-engineer
Summary: The skills a software engineer needs in 2026, which ones decide the offer, and how to check your own resume against a real software engineering job.

- SkillDrift
- Skills by role
- Software Engineer
## Skills needed for a software engineer in 2026
A software engineer needs one or two programming languages used to a professional standard, the tools of modern delivery such as version control, testing and cloud deployment, system design, and the human skills of working in a team. The weight of each changes with the role and the seniority.
Check yours against a real software engineer job. Most engineers who reach an interview have the core list. What separates them is usually further down it, and in how clearly the resume shows it.
## Start with your resume.
Takes about a minute
Upload it once. You get your readiness score, your closest roles, your real gaps and week one of a plan built for them.
Drop your resume here
PDF, DOC or DOCX · up to 5 MB · takes about a minute
Get my readiness score
We read your resume to score it and find matches. We store it so you don’t have to upload it again if you make an account, and delete it after 30 days if you don’t. Privacy policy.
Don’t have a resume? Build one with SkillDrift AI in 2 minutes. Build my resume
Technical skills
## Technical skills most postings ask for
### One or two languages in depth
Python, Java, JavaScript or TypeScript, Go and C# cover most postings. Depth in one beats a long list.
### Data structures and algorithms
Still tested in most interviews and still used in daily work.
### Version control and code review
Git, pull requests, and changes someone else can read.
### Testing
Unit and integration tests, and knowing what is worth testing.
### Cloud and deployment
One cloud platform, containers, and how code reaches production.
### Databases
SQL first, then one non relational store and when to use it.
### System design
How services talk, fail and scale. It grows with seniority.
### Working with AI tools
Using assistants to write, review and test code, and knowing when they are wrong.
Human skills
## Human skills that postings ask for
### Written communication
Clear tickets, design notes, review comments and incident write ups.
### Ownership
Taking something from an idea to production and keeping it running.
### Collaboration
Working with product, design and other engineers without friction.
What decides the offer
## The skills that decide the offer
Most people who reach the interview have the core list. These are the skills that usually separate them.
### Communication
In the SkillDrift Jobs Index, communication is still one of the most requested skills across job postings. For engineers it means review comments that teach and design notes a new joiner can follow.
### Ownership, idea to production
A posting that says end to end is asking whether you have shipped something and kept it running. Many engineers have done this and describe it as worked on the backend.
### Working with AI
Postings now ask for engineers who can direct AI tools, check their output and stay accountable for the result.
On your resume
## How to show these skills on your resume
The same work, but the second line shows system design, observability, documentation and ownership. A screening system matches words, so a skill that is not written down is a skill that does not count.
### Before
Developed backend services in Java.
### After
Designed and ran a payments service in Java, including alerting, runbooks and on call.

By title
## Software developer or software engineer?
In most postings the two titles mean the same job. Where they differ, the engineer title leans more on system design, reliability and scale, and the developer title on building features inside an existing system. Choose your skills by the posting you want, not by the title.
FAQ
## Questions people ask
What skills are needed for a software engineer?
One or two programming languages in depth, version control, testing, cloud and deployment, databases, system design, working with AI tools, and written communication. The mix depends on the role and the seniority.
What are the software developer required skills for a first job?
One language used well, data structures and algorithms, Git, basic testing and SQL. Show one project you built and ran from start to finish.
Which skill most often costs a software engineer the offer?
Rarely the language. More often it is communication, ownership or system design that the resume does not show and the interview then tests.
How do I check my skills against a software engineering job?
Upload your resume to SkillDrift and pick the job. It names the skills the posting asks for that your resume does not show, scores the job out of 100, and builds a learning path for each gap.

# Teacher Skills: What the Job Asks For in 2026 | SkillDrift
URL: https://www.skilldrift.ai/skills/teacher
Summary: The skills a teacher needs in 2026, from lesson planning to classroom management and assessment, which ones decide the offer, and how to check your own gap.

- SkillDrift
- Skills by role
- Teacher
## Teacher skills in 2026
A teacher needs strong knowledge of their subject, the ability to plan lessons that build on each other, classroom management, assessment that shows what each student has learned, and differentiation so that students at different levels can all make progress. Schools also ask for confident use of education technology and clear communication with parents and colleagues. Patience and care for students matter in every part of the job.
Check yours against a real teacher job. Most teaching resumes list the subjects and age groups taught. The offer usually turns on whether the resume shows how students progressed, and how the teacher knew.
## Start with your resume.
Takes about a minute
Upload it once. You get your readiness score, your closest roles, your real gaps and week one of a plan built for them.
Drop your resume here
PDF, DOC or DOCX · up to 5 MB · takes about a minute
Get my readiness score
We read your resume to score it and find matches. We store it so you don’t have to upload it again if you make an account, and delete it after 30 days if you don’t. Privacy policy.
Don’t have a resume? Build one with SkillDrift AI in 2 minutes. Build my resume
Technical skills
## Teaching skills most postings ask for
### Subject knowledge
Knowing the subject well enough to explain it in more than one way and to answer unexpected questions.
### Lesson planning
Lessons with a clear goal, in a sequence that builds over a term.
### Classroom management
Setting routines and expectations so that the class can focus on learning.
### Assessment
Using quizzes, tasks and questions to check understanding, then changing the next lesson based on what you find.
### Differentiation
Adapting tasks and support so that students at different levels, including students with additional needs, can all make progress.
### Education technology
A learning management system, presentation tools and online resources, and running a lesson online when needed.
Human skills
## Human skills that decide the classroom
### Communication with parents
Explaining progress and concerns clearly and respectfully, in meetings and in writing.
### Patience
Explaining an idea again, in a new way, for a student who has not understood it yet.
### Working with colleagues
Sharing plans and resources, and agreeing assessment standards with other teachers.
### Reflection
Reviewing what worked in a lesson and changing the next one.
What decides the offer
## The skills that decide the offer
Most people who reach the interview have the core list. These are the skills that usually separate them.
### Classroom management in practice
Interviews often include a demonstration lesson or a question about behaviour. A calm, specific answer about routines and follow up carries more weight than general principles.
### Evidence of progress
Schools want teachers who can show how they know students are learning. Describe one way you tracked progress and what you changed as a result.
### Meeting different needs
Interviewers often ask how you would support a student who is far ahead of the class or far behind it. A concrete example of differentiation stands out.
On your resume
## How to show these skills on your resume
The second line shows planning, assessment, differentiation and a result. Use your own real results. A screening system matches words, so a skill that is not written down is a skill that does not count.
### Before
Taught mathematics to students aged 12 to 14.
### After
Planned and taught mathematics to three classes aged 12 to 14, used short weekly quizzes to find gaps, and regrouped students for targeted practice, which raised end of term results in all three classes.

- Ready for the interview Practise the teacher interview out loud and get an honest score out of 10, with the weak answers turned into a plan.
By title
## Teaching assistant, teacher and head of department skills
A teaching assistant role leans on supporting individual students and small groups, and on following the plan of the lead teacher. A teacher role adds lesson planning, assessment and full responsibility for a class. A head of department or lead teacher role adds planning the curriculum for a subject, guiding other teachers and reviewing results. The step up is usually decided by evidence that you improved results beyond your own classes.
FAQ
## Questions people ask
What skills does a teacher need?
Subject knowledge, lesson planning, classroom management, assessment, differentiation, education technology, clear communication with parents and colleagues, and patience.
What teacher skills should I put on my resume?
Name the subjects and age groups you taught, the assessment and technology tools you used, and one result that shows students progressed. Add classroom management and communication, each backed by a line in your experience.
What skills help someone move into teaching from another career?
Subject knowledge from the previous job, experience of explaining ideas to others through training or mentoring, and organisation. Most schools also require a recognised teaching qualification for the place where they are based.
How do I check my skills against a teaching job?
Upload your resume to SkillDrift and pick the job. It names the skills the posting asks for that your resume does not show, scores the job out of 100, and builds a learning path for each gap.

# Skills Employers Ask For in Data and AI Jobs, October 2026 | SkillDrift
URL: https://www.skilldrift.ai/skills/in-demand/data-ai-jobs
Summary: The skills named most often in 33,406 data and AI jobs: SQL, Python, Data analysis, Power BI. Live job index data, and a way to check your own resume against them.

- SkillDrift

How to read this
## Where these numbers come from
The SkillDrift job index collects live job postings and reads the skills each one asks for. This page counts the postings in the engineering role group within the real estate industry, and shows the share that name each skill. Skills appear as employers write them, so close variants such as Excel and MS Excel can both appear, because a posting may use either. The page is refreshed from the index, and the date above shows the last read.

1,066 postings, read from the SkillDrift job index on 1 October 2026. Each share is the number of postings that name the skill, divided by all postings in this group.

### Why check this in SkillDrift?
- Real jobs in this field, scored for you Each one scored out of 100 against your resume, with the skills you already show and the ones to close named.
- A plan that moves your scores Learning built for each gap and sized to your hours. Finish it and the certificate goes into your resume, and the jobs that ask for that skill move up.
- Ready for the interview Practise the real interview out loud and get an honest score out of 10, with the weak answers turned into a plan.

How to read this
## Where these numbers come from
The SkillDrift job index collects live job postings and reads the skills each one asks for. This page counts the postings in the sales role group within the software industry, and shows the share that name each skill. Skills appear as employers write them, so close variants such as Excel and MS Excel can both appear, because a posting may use either. The page is refreshed from the index, and the date above shows the last read.
FAQ
## Questions people ask
What is the most requested skill in sales jobs in software?
Negotiation. It is named in 31.4% of the 4,820 sales jobs in software in the SkillDrift job index on 1 October 2026.
How many job postings is this based on?
4,820 postings, read from the SkillDrift job index on 1 October 2026. Each share is the number of postings that name the skill, divided by all postings in this group.

## Privacy Policy
How we collect, use, share and protect your information, and the choices you have over it.
Effective Date/Last Modified: 6th June 2025
## Overview
This Privacy Policy describes:
- Information that we receive from you when you interact with the Services
- How we use and process the information that we receive
- If and why Personal Information may be disclosed to third parties
- Your choices regarding the collection and processing of your Personal Information
Please note that this Privacy Policy does not apply to information collected through third-party websites or services that you may access through the Services or that you submit to us through e-mail, text message, other electronic message or offline.
PLEASE REVIEW THIS PRIVACY POLICY CAREFULLY.
When you submit information to or through the Services, you consent to the collection and processing of your information as described in this Privacy Policy.
By using the Services, you accept the terms of this Privacy Policy and our Terms of Use and consent to our collection, use, disclosure and retention of your information as described in this Privacy Policy.
This Privacy Policy is incorporated into and made a part of our Terms of Use.
IF YOU DO NOT AGREE WITH ANY PART OF THIS PRIVACY POLICY OR OUR TERMS OF USE, PLEASE DO NOT USE ANY OF THE SERVICES.
The Effective Date of this Privacy Policy is set forth at the top of this Policy. Whenever possible, we will provide you with advance written notice of our changes to this Privacy Policy. We will not make retroactive changes that reduce your privacy rights unless we are legally required to do so. Your continued use of the Services after the Effective Date constitutes your acceptance of the amended Privacy Policy. The amended Privacy Policy supersedes all previous versions.
## 1. Information We Collect
### Types of Information
We collect various kinds of information that you provide to us as well as information we obtain from your use of the Services. Some of the types of information that we collect include:
"Personal Information"
Information associated with or used to identify or contact a specific person. Personal Information includes:
- Contact data (such as e-mail address, telephone number and employer)
- Demographic data (such as gender, date of birth and zip code)
- Certain Usage Data (defined below), such as IP address
- Your current skillsets derived using AI from your on & off job activities as mentioned in your resume or LinkedIn profile and any such information that you agree to share with us through your personnel website among others
- Your aspirations that you agree to share with us
- Your educational background including the certificates that you may upload on our platform from time to time
Certain Personal Information, such as information about personal health or finances, is characterized as Sensitive and subject to stricter regulation than other personal information. Before providing it to use, we urge you to carefully consider whether to disclose your Sensitive Personal Information to us. If you do provide Sensitive Personal Information to us, you consent to its use and disclosure for the purposes and in the manner described in this Privacy Policy.
"Usage Data"
Information about an individual's online activity that, by itself, does not identify the individual, such as:
- Technical information, including your browser type, service provider, IP address, operating system and webpages visited
- Information about what you've searched for and looked at while using the Services
- Metadata, which means information related to items you made available through the Services, such as the date, time or location that a shared photograph or video was taken or posted
(Generally, we do not consider Usage Data as Personal Information because Usage Data by itself usually does not identify an individual. Personal Information and Usage Data may be linked together. Different types of Usage Information also may be linked together and, once linked, may identify an individual person. Some Usage Data may be Personal Information under applicable law.)
"Location Data"
A category of Personal Information collected about the location of a mobile device or computer, including:
- The location of the mobile device or computer used to access the Services derived from GPS or WiFi use
- The IP address of the mobile device or computer or internet service used to access the Services
- Other information made available by a user or others that indicates the current or prior location of the user, such as information that you or others post indicating your location or geotag information in photographs
## 2. How We Collect Information
Whether we collect certain types of information and how we process it depends on how you use and access the Services. Some information is collected automatically through use of cookies and similar data collection tools. We collect information about you in the following ways:
### From You
We collect information from you when you:
- Use the Services. We collect Personal Information from you when you create an account to use one of the Services, contact us for help or information or otherwise voluntarily provide your Personal Information. We collect the information and content that you submit to us, such as when you enter comments or submit a review.
- Connect with social media though the Services. The Services may offer you the ability to use Facebook Connect or other social media services (collectively, "social media") in conjunction with certain Services. When you access the Services through your Facebook or other Social Media account, the Services may, depending on your privacy settings, have access to information that you have provided to the Social Media platform. We may use this information for the purposes described in this Privacy Policy or at the time the information was collected.
### From Our Business Partners and Service Providers
Third parties that assist us with our business operations also collect information (including Personal Information and Usage Data) about you through the Services and share it with us. For example, our vendors collect and share information with us to help us detect and prevent fraud.
We may combine the information we collect from you with information from other sources and use the combined information as described in this Privacy Policy.
### Usage Data
We also automatically collect Usage Data when you interact with the Services.
### From cookies and other data collection tools
We, along with the service providers that help us provide the Services, use small text files called "cookies", which are small computer files sent to or accessed from your web browser or your computer's or tablet's hard drive that contain information about your computer, such as a user ID, user settings, browsing history and activities conducted while using the Services. Cookies are not themselves personally identifiable, but may be linked to Personal Information that you provide to us through your interaction with the Services.
Cookies help us improve the Services by tracking users' navigation habits and storing users' password, customizing users' experience with the Services; enabling us to analyze technical and navigational information about the Services; and helping to detect and prevent fraud.
We also use other cookies and other data collection tools (such as web beacons and server logs), which we collectively refer to as "data collection tools," to help improve your experience with the Services.
Web browsers allow some control of most cookies through the browser settings. To find out more about cookies, including how to manage and delete cookies, visit www.allaboutcookies.org. Although users are not required to accept cookies or mobile device identifiers, blocking or rejecting them may prevent access to some features available through the Services.
## Resumes uploaded without an account
You can upload a resume on our website without signing in or creating an account. We process that file to produce your readiness score, the skill gaps holding it down and your matched roles, and we show them to you in place. We do not email you as a result of that upload.
The upload creates a temporary guest session, identified by a token held in your browser's local storage. That session lasts 48 hours, after which it expires and the results can no longer be retrieved. If you create an account or sign in while the session is still live, the resume and the analysis generated from it are transferred to your account, and are from that point covered by the rest of this Privacy Policy.
If you never create an account, the uploaded file and everything derived from it are deleted within 30 days.
### Limits on this upload
- Accepted formats are PDF, DOC and DOCX, up to 5 MB per file
- Uploads are rate limited by IP address to protect the service from abuse
- One analysis is produced per upload; uploading again starts a new session
To stop automated abuse of this upload we use Google reCAPTCHA v3, which collects hardware and software information from your device and browser and sends it to Google for analysis. Your use of reCAPTCHA is subject to Google's Privacy Policy and Terms of Service.

We may use the information we collect for any of the following purposes:
- To provide the Services to you
- To operate, improve and personalize the products and services we offer, and to give each user a more consistent and personalized experience when interacting with us
- For customer service, security, to detect fraud or illegal activities, or for archival and backup purposes in connection with the provision of the Services
- To communicate with users
- To better understand how users access and use the Services, for the purposes of trying to improve the Services and to respond to user preferences, including language and location customization, personalized help and instructions, or other responses to users' usage of the Services
- To help us develop our new products and services and improve our existing products and services
- To provide users with advertising and direct marketing that is more relevant to you
- To enforce our Terms of Use or other applicable policies
- To assess the effectiveness of and improve advertising and other marketing and promotional activities on or in connection with the Services
Please note that, in order to provide you with a better experience and to improve the Services, information collected through the Services may be used in an aggregated or individualized manner.
For example, personal information collected during use of one of the services may be used to suggest particular content that can be made available to the user on another of the Services or be used to try to present more relevant advertising in another of the Services.

### For legal purposes

We will disclose Personal Information as we deem necessary to respond to a subpoena, regulation, binding order of a data protection agency, legal process, governmental request or other legal or regulatory process. We may also share Personal Information as required to pursue available remedies or limit damages we may sustain.
### In aggregated form
We may share Personal Information about you in an aggregated form - that is, in a statistical or summary form that does not include any personal identifiers - with third parties in order to discover and reveal trends about how users like you interact with our services.
### With Mobile Platform Providers
We share necessary data with Apple (for iOS users) and Google (for Android users) to facilitate in-app purchases, analytics, and app store compliance.
### During corporate changes

When one of these events occurs, we will use reasonable efforts to notify users before your information is transferred or becomes subject to a different privacy policy.

## Data Protection Policy
Learn how we protect and handle your personal and professional data
Last Updated: June 11, 2025
SkillDrift, Inc. ("SkillDrift," "we," "our," or "us") is committed to protecting your personal data and respecting your privacy rights. This Data Protection Policy explains how we collect, process, store, and protect your personal and professional information in accordance with applicable data protection laws, including the General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR), California Consumer Privacy Act (CCPA), and other relevant privacy regulations.
As an AI-native Talent Mobility platform, we process professional data to provide skill intelligence, career pathing, and talent matching services. This policy outlines our commitment to responsible data handling and your rights regarding your information.
## 1. Data Controller Information
SkillDrift, Inc. acts as the data controller for the personal data we process through our platform and services.
Company: SkillDrift, Inc.
Email: sales@skilldrift.ai
Data Protection Officer: legal@skilldrift.ai
## 2. Types of Data We Collect
### Personal Information
- Identity Data: First name, last name, username, professional title
- Contact Data: Email address, telephone number, location, employer information
- Account Data: Login credentials, account preferences, subscription details
### Professional and Career Data
- Resume and CV Information: Work experience, education, certifications, achievements
- LinkedIn Profile Data: Professional background, connections, endorsements (with your consent)
- Skill Profiles: Current skills, competency levels, skill gaps identified by our AI
- Career Aspirations: Goals, preferences, desired career paths
- Learning Progress: Courses completed, certifications earned, training activities
- Performance Data: Assessments, feedback, and evaluation results (where applicable)
### Technical and Usage Data
- Technical Data: IP address, browser type, device information, operating system
- Usage Data: Platform interactions, feature usage, session duration, click patterns
- AI Interaction Data: Queries to our AI systems, generated insights, recommendation interactions
- Integration Data: Information from connected HR systems, learning platforms, and third-party services
### Enterprise Customer Data
- Organizational Data: Company structure, team hierarchies, role definitions
- Workforce Analytics: Aggregated skill inventories, talent pipeline data, succession planning information
- HR System Data: Employee records, performance reviews, training records (as authorized by employers)
## 3. How We Collect Data
- Direct Collection: Information you provide when creating accounts, uploading resumes, or using platform features
- Third-Party Integrations: Data from LinkedIn, HR systems (Workday, SAP), learning platforms (Coursera, Udemy)
- AI Analysis: Skill profiles and insights generated from your professional information
- Platform Usage: Automatically collected technical and behavioral data
- Enterprise Systems: Data shared by employers for workforce planning and talent mobility
## 4. Legal Basis for Processing
We process your personal data based on the following legal grounds:
- Consent: When you provide explicit consent for specific processing activities, such as AI skill analysis or third-party integrations
- Contract Performance: To provide our talent mobility services, skill matching, and career development tools
- Legitimate Interests: For platform improvement, fraud prevention, and providing relevant career opportunities
- Legal Obligations: To comply with employment law, data protection regulations, and other legal requirements
- Employer Authorization: When processing employee data as authorized by enterprise customers for workforce planning
## 5. How We Use Your Data
### AI-Powered Services
- Generate comprehensive skill profiles from your professional experience
- Identify skill gaps and recommend learning opportunities
- Match you with relevant career opportunities and job openings
- Provide personalized career path recommendations
- Create tailored resumes and professional documents
### Platform Operations
- Provide access to our talent mobility platform and features
- Maintain and improve service functionality
- Provide customer support and technical assistance
- Process payments and manage subscriptions
- Ensure platform security and prevent fraud
### Enterprise Services
- Workforce planning and strategic talent alignment
- Internal talent discovery and mobility facilitation
- Skills gap analysis and training recommendations
- Succession planning and leadership development
- HR analytics and reporting dashboards
## 6. Data Sharing and Disclosure
We only share your data in the following circumstances:
- With Your Consent: When you explicitly authorize data sharing with potential employers or learning partners
- Service Providers: With trusted third-party vendors who help us operate our platform (cloud storage, analytics, payment processing)
- Enterprise Customers: Within your organization for internal mobility and workforce planning (for employee users)
- Legal Requirements: When required by law, court order, or to protect our legal rights
- Business Transfers: In connection with mergers, acquisitions, or asset sales (with user notification)
We never sell your personal data to third parties.
## 7. AI and Automated Decision Making
Our platform uses artificial intelligence to provide personalized insights and recommendations. Here's how we ensure responsible AI use:
- Transparency: We provide explanations for AI-generated recommendations and skill assessments
- Human Oversight: AI insights are designed to assist, not replace, human decision-making
- Bias Prevention: We regularly audit our algorithms for fairness and work to eliminate discriminatory outcomes
- User Control: You can review, correct, and provide feedback on AI-generated insights
- No Fully Automated Decisions: Significant decisions (hiring, promotions) always involve human review
## 8. Data Security Measures
We implement comprehensive security measures to protect your data:
- Encryption: Data encrypted in transit (TLS 1.3) and at rest (AES-256)
- Access Controls: Role-based access controls and multi-factor authentication
- Infrastructure Security: Secure cloud hosting with regular security audits
- Employee Training: Regular data protection and security training for all staff
- Incident Response: Comprehensive breach detection and response procedures
- Regular Audits: Third-party security assessments and penetration testing
- Data Backups: Secure, encrypted backup systems with tested recovery procedures
## 9. Data Retention
We retain your data for different periods based on the type of information and purpose:
- Account Data: Retained while your account is active and for 30 days after account deletion
- Professional Data: Retained as long as your account is active and for 30 days after account deletion
- Usage Data: Typically retained for 2 years for analytics and platform improvement
- AI Training Data: Anonymized data may be retained longer for model improvement
- Legal Requirements: Some data may be retained longer to comply with legal obligations
When data is no longer needed, we securely delete or anonymize it using industry-standard methods.
## 10. Your Privacy Rights
You have the following rights regarding your personal data:
- Right of Access: Request copies of your personal data and information about how it's processed
- Right to Rectification: Request correction of inaccurate or incomplete data
- Right to Erasure: Request deletion of your personal data (subject to legal requirements)
- Right to Restrict Processing: Limit how we use your data in certain circumstances
- Right to Data Portability: Receive your data in a structured format for transfer to another service
- Right to Object: Object to processing based on legitimate interests or for marketing purposes
- Right to Withdraw Consent: Withdraw consent for specific processing activities
- Right to Human Review: Request human review of automated decisions that significantly affect you
To exercise these rights, contact us at legal@skilldrift.ai. We will respond within 30 days.
## 11. How to Delete Your Account
You can permanently delete your SkillDrift account by following these steps:
### Step-by-Step Account Deletion Process:
- Log into your SkillDrift account using your credentials
- Navigate to Settings by clicking on your profile menu and selecting "Settings"
- Go to the Account section within the Settings menu
- Scroll to the bottom of the Account page where you will find account management options
- Click on "Delete Account" option at the bottom of the page
- Follow the confirmation prompts to permanently delete your account and associated data
⚠️ Important Notes:
- Account deletion is permanent and cannot be undone
- All your personal data will be deleted within 30 days of account deletion
- Some data may be retained longer if required by legal obligations
- Downloaded reports or shared data with third parties may not be automatically deleted
If you encounter any issues during the account deletion process, please contact our support team at legal@skilldrift.ai for assistance.
## 12. International Data Transfers
SkillDrift operates globally and may transfer your data across international borders. When we do so, we ensure appropriate safeguards:
- Adequacy Decisions: Transfers to countries with adequate data protection laws
- Standard Contractual Clauses: EU-approved contractual protections for other transfers
- Enterprise Controls: Additional safeguards for enterprise customer data
- Data Residency Options: Regional data storage options for enterprise customers
## 13. Cookies and Tracking Technologies
We use cookies and similar technologies to enhance your experience:
- Essential Cookies: Required for platform functionality and security
- Analytics Cookies: Help us understand platform usage and improve services
- Preference Cookies: Remember your settings and personalization choices
- Third-Party Cookies: From integrated services like LinkedIn or learning platforms
You can control cookie settings through your browser preferences or our cookie consent manager.
## 14. Children's Privacy
Our services are not intended for individuals under 18 years of age. We do not knowingly collect personal information from children under 18. If we become aware that we have collected such information, we will take steps to delete it promptly.
## 15. Changes to This Policy
We may update this Data Protection Policy to reflect changes in our practices or applicable laws. We will notify you of material changes by:
- Email notification to registered users
- Prominent notice on our platform
- Updated effective date on this policy
Continued use of our services after changes constitutes acceptance of the updated policy.
## 16. Contact Information
For questions about this Data Protection Policy, to exercise your privacy rights, or to report concerns:
Data Protection Officer: legal@skilldrift.ai
General Support: sales@skilldrift.ai
Website: www.skilldrift.ai
Response Time: We aim to respond to all privacy-related inquiries within 30 days.
If you are not satisfied with our response to your privacy concerns, you have the right to lodge a complaint with your local data protection authority or supervisory authority.
